In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CARD9–NOD2 interaction involves the linker between CARDs and NACTH of NOD2, as well as NACTH of both NOD2 and of CARD9.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NOD2 and its adaptor CARD9 form a complex in the cytosol that can activate the p38 and JNK MAPKs in response to muramyl di peptide.
NOD2 and the adaptor protein CARD are able to interact through two sites in the NOD2 molecule, and this interaction is important for NOD2‐mediated immune signalling.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the NACHT of NOD2 is an important interaction site with CARD9 and that the CARD–NACT linker is a novel interaction site for CARD9.
NOD2 is a multi‐domain protein and the NACHT domain is not only involved in the recognition of the bacterial product muramyl di‐peptide but also in the recruitment of CARD9 to the NOD2 complex.
the NACHT domain, and in particular the linker region connecting the CARDs and NACHT, plays an important role in NOD2 signalling.
